The Academic Staff Union of Polytechnics, Zone C, has directed all its chapters across state-owned polytechnics, colleges of technology, and monotechnics in Ogun, Oyo, Osun, and Ekiti states to embark on an industrial strike over the non-implementation of the Consolidated Academic Tools Allowance and Earned Academic Allowance. This was contained in a statement signed by the Zonal Executive Council of ASUP Zone C and read by its coordinator, Masopa, Adekunle Nurudeen, during a press conference held at the ASUP Secretariat, The Polytechnic, Ibadan, the Oyo State capital, on Thursday. The union lamented that while the Federal Government had commenced the payment of CATA and EAA to academic staff in Federal institutions on the CONPCASS salary structure, state governments in the zone—with the exception of Ondo State—had failed to follow suit. Nurudeen stated that the strike action took effect on Monday, November 16, 2026, following the expiration of a 15-day ultimatum issued to state governments across the South-West zone. According to the union, “The Federal Government concluded the renegotiation of the 2009/2010 agreement with ASUP in April 2026 under the Yayale Ahmed-led committee, birthing the 2025/2026 FGN/ASUP Agreement with an effective implementation date of January 1, 2026. Tinubu, South-West govs invited to Adeleke’s second-term inauguration Diaspora doctors seek medical missions to strengthen healthcare in Nigeria Adeleke appoints new monarch for Esa-Oke “Following the lack of response, ASUP resolved at its 118th National Executive Council meeting held in Abuja between October 23 and 24, 2026, to issue a 15-day ultimatum to defaulting state governments, which elapsed on Tuesday, November 10, 2026. “We are now directing all our chapters across state-owned polytechnics, colleges of technology, and monotechnics in Ogun, Oyo, Osun, and Ekiti states to embark on an industrial strike over the non-implementation of the Consolidated Academic Tools Allowance and Earned Academic Allowance.” While commending the Ondo State Government as the first and only state in the zone to implement the 2025/2026 agreement, ASUP criticised the governments of Ogun, Oyo, Osun, and Ekiti states for their silence. “State governments should endeavour to treat our members in state-owned institutions appropriately, not as second-class citizens within the same national economy,” the union demanded. ASUP Zone C listed its core demands to include the immediate implementation of CATA and EAA for academic staff in state-owned polytechnics, colleges of technology, and monotechnics across Ogun, Oyo, Osun, and Ekiti states, as well as the payment of accrued arrears from January 1, 2026, to date. “Considering the unimpressive and demoralising conduct of the state governments of Ogun, Oyo, Osun, and Ekiti on the implementation of CATA and EAA, which has resulted in the non-implementation of these allowances, the Zonal Executive Council hereby reiterates the directive of the National Executive Council at the 118th NEC meeting; hence, we have directed all state chapters of ASUP to proceed on industrial strike effective from Monday, November 16, 2026,” the statement concluded.
